facts.text: Elsinore was named by Danish settlers after Kronborg Castle, the historic home of Shakespeare’s Hamlet, reflecting the town’s Danish roots.
The first passenger train rolled into Elsinore on July 21, 1896, linking the town to the Denver & Rio Grande Railroad.
From 1911 to 1929, Elsinore housed a Utah‑Idaho Sugar Company factory that processed sugar beets until a blight forced its closure.
In late September and early October 1921, Elsinore trembled under two magnitude‑six earthquakes, damaging buildings but sparing lives.
Elsinore’s first library began in the basement of its public school, starting with a modest collection of 1,000 books.
Today, Elsinore supports local artists through a small gallery and gift shop that showcases regional talent.
